evals.prompt: Inspect the current Shepherd skill and prove role ownership is clear: coordinator coordinates, implementer implements behavior slices and architect-finding repairs, refactorer refactors, architect hardens and runs mutation.
evals.expected_output: The Shepherd source and prompts contain the role split, architect-owned hardening/mutation, no active reviewer prompt references, and no coordinator-owned mutation language.

evals.prompt: Run a tiny fixture with normal acceptance, source mutation, and acceptance-spec mutation where all mutants are killed.
evals.expected_output: Unit tests and normal acceptance run separately; architect hardening records source and acceptance mutation reports and approves the milestone.

evals.prompt: Run a tiny fixture where generated acceptance tests still pass after mutating an example value.
evals.expected_output: Architect hardening records the survivor path and requests focused implementer repair instead of approving the milestone.

evals.prompt: Run a tiny fixture where acceptance-spec mutation infrastructure fails while normal acceptance passes.
evals.expected_output: Architect hardening treats the mutation error as unverifiable infrastructure and requests focused implementer repair.

evals.prompt: Run a tiny fixture where source-code mutation has a survivor while acceptance-spec mutation is killed.
evals.expected_output: Architect hardening records source mutation separately from acceptance-spec mutation and requests focused implementer repair.

evals.prompt: Run a tiny fixture with no useful acceptance-spec mutations.
evals.expected_output: Architect hardening blocks approval because the acceptance examples cannot prove behavior-relevant binding.

evals.prompt: Exercise the Shepherd live-code playground with a real code and test diff.
evals.expected_output: The playground captures before/after test output and a concrete code diff proving the evaluated workflow touched real implementation behavior.
